newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on stronger Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on stronger Chicago.

text.p: All Tokyo corn futures closed higher on Tuesday, due to a stronger Chicago corn market overnight, as short covering by local investors pushed up nearby months in particular, traders said.
Prices were 50 to 280 yen per tonne higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract closing 50 yen up at 14,450 yen. The day's estimated volume was 57,745 lots.

All months rallied from the opening, on buying from local investors, traders said. The spot July expires on June 13. "Some local investors actively covered short positions ahead of the spot month's expiry," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.74-3/4 per bushel at 0810 GMT, up from $2.74 at Monday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.73-1/2 a bushel at 0810 GMT, against $8.75-1/4 at Monday's close.
